title: Visualizing flat-band spatial renormalization in rhombohedral graphene superlattices
authors: Peng-Cheng Pan, Shihao Zhang, Yang Zhang, Ji Huang, Ling-Hui Tong, Chen-Chen Xu, Yuan Tian, Li Zhang, Lijie Zhang, Yuanyuan Hu, Wen-Xiao Wang, Zhihui Qin, Long-Jing Yin
abstract: Rhombohedral graphene/hBN moiré superlattices exhibit flat-band-driven emergent phases, including superconductivity and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (FQAHE), yet the microscopic role of the moiré potential remains unclear. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy, we visualize moiré-modulated spatial renormalization of flat bands in rhombohedral pentalayer and tetralayer graphene/hBN superlattices. We observe spatially hierarchical filling, manifested as periodic energy shifts of the flat bands at the moiré scale, leading to spatial reshaping of correlated states in the interacting regime. Remarkably, this modulation vanishes below a ~10 nm moiré period--the same threshold below which the FQAHE is absent. Theoretical modeling attributes this mechanism to atomic-corrugation-induced charge redistribution. Our work provides real-space visualization of moiré-engineered flat-band reconstruction, resolving a key link between moiré periodic potential and emergent topological order.
summary: This work uses STM to visualize how the moiré potential in graphene/hBN superlattices causes a periodic, site-dependent renormalization of flat electronic bands. The key finding is that this spatial modulation only exists above a critical moiré period ($\sim 10 	ext{ nm}$), establishing a direct, real-space link between the moiré potential and the emergence of topological order like the FQAHE.
main_problem: The study aims to clarify the microscopic role of the moiré potential in driving emergent correlated phases, such as the Fractional Quantum Anomalous Hall Effect (FQAHE), in rhombohedral graphene superlattices.
main_result: The authors visualize that the moiré potential causes a spatially periodic renormalization of flat bands, and this modulation vanishes below a critical moiré period ($\sim 10 	ext{ nm}$), which coincides with the threshold for FQAHE.
method: The research combines Scanning Tunneling Microscopy/Spectroscopy (STM/STS) to image real-space electronic structure with theoretical modeling to attribute the modulation to atomic corrugation-induced charge redistribution.
model_or_system: The system studied is rhombohedral graphene (RG) superlattices formed with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) substrates (e.g., R4G/hBN, R5G/hBN). The physics involves flat-band physics, correlated electron behavior, and the formation of topological states.
key_observables: Spatially resolved energy shifts of flat bands ($	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$ spectra), the magnitude of the band splitting gap ($\Delta$), and the persistence of moiré-scale modulation.
important_parameters: Moiré period ($\lambda_m$), which shows a critical threshold around $10 	ext{ nm}$; the filling level (full vs. partial); and the twist angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The mechanism driving the modulation is theoretically attributed to atomic corrugation inducing a spatially varying local chemical potential.
figures_summary: Figures show STM topography and spatially resolved $	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$ spectra demonstrating site-dependent energy shifts. They illustrate the disappearance of this modulation when the moiré period is too small, and map the spatial reshaping of correlated states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the importance of moiré-driven phases. It then uses STM/STS to observe the spatial renormalization of flat bands, demonstrating the dependence on the moiré period. Finally, it links this observed periodicity threshold to the theoretical requirement for topological order.
why_interesting: The direct visualization of how a geometric potential (the moiré pattern) dictates the emergence of topological order in a correlated system provides a concrete, experimentally verifiable mechanism for realizing exotic quantum states.
